title: Price compatible width menus and resolve the rank-12 dispatch frontier
body:
## Result

This answers the priced-menu follow-up in Nick Petalas's #6658. Given a finite compatible menu at each chronological cut and an exact price per invocation, the package characterizes every nondominated choice of replication and normalized cost. It proves the **least eventual period of the total excess charge and the exact replication where that periodic tail begins**, including permanently infeasible residues and cases where one cut masks another's early exceptions. [Source handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6658) · [Proof](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e90d4e3cb77ed31c259b902e7aad9598c89327b5/research/priced-width-frontier/PROOF.md)

For the existing rank-12 toy flow of Mihir Srivastava's #4507, I offered both compiled widths at each child rank, retained the source leaf counts and assigned **one additional unit per positive-rank child dispatch at the parent**. The 515 separate child cuts yield only two Pareto points.

| Replication | Productive width | Normalized charge |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 700 | 110,600 | 349039/27650 |
| 2,744,000 | 433,552,000 | 684112521/54194000 |

The first 3,919 feasible replications cost the same per productive unit. At the floor, increasing replication by a factor of 3,920 saves exactly **3919/54194000** per productive unit. One rank-eight nested invocation replaces 3,920 smaller ones at the same leaf cost. If its surcharge equals or exceeds their combined surcharge, replication 700 is the sole Pareto point. The unit fee is a model assumption. [Full invoice, original programs and price threshold](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e90d4e3cb77ed31c259b902e7aad9598c89327b5/research/priced-width-frontier/RANK12.md) · [#4507](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4507)

Charging every positive invocation inside both fixed historical child libraries gives the same two replication choices. A literal traversal visits 3,639 and 13,928,545 calls in their rank-eight programs. Replacing 3,920 narrow calls by one nested call saves 336,335 invocations per rank-eight cut. The normalized saving becomes 67267/10838800. [Recursive invoice](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e90d4e3cb77ed31c259b902e7aad9598c89327b5/research/priced-width-frontier/RANK12.md#charging-every-internal-call-of-the-two-fixed-libraries)

A second family has an unbounded number of Pareto points despite only four programs and the same one-unit fee. At widths 12 and 13 it has ten records, ending at replication 156. A tied-price family shows that the last exception of an individual cut can grow quadratically even when the combined excess sequence is periodic from the start.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/priced-width-frontier
```

- Compared 1,023 distinct single-cut menus against direct amount optimization and 107,403 literal count vectors. Compared all 292,995 unordered pairs in a separate finite grid, covering 17,579,700 positive pair/replication observations. In 5,319 pairs the joint onset preceded the larger of the two individual onsets.
- Recomputed the #4507 toy compiler inputs, compared all 3,920 feasible replications through the first cost floor with an independent invoice, and checked both strict sides and equality of the rank-eight fee boundary. A separate run disabled the compressed compiler, enumerated the original target words and paid paths, and independently recovered all 515 cuts and both cost frontiers. Executed 12 small charged shear schedules and checked every output coordinate.
- Normal and optimized Python returned identical scientific receipts. Twenty actual private-copy mutations failed for their specified reasons in both modes. The official source-history and export checks passed in a separate full-history clone. The read-only export, SHA-256 `22d533a78dc59fcf5ee2a3ec7684f350329a153caa98a04ef55b9019ea2c8f5b`, replayed normal, optimized, census, literal-source and mutation checks with all exported files unchanged. [Validation details](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e90d4e3cb77ed31c259b902e7aad9598c89327b5/research/priced-width-frontier/VALIDATION.md)

## Checks on the published head

GitHub canceled the upstream planning job after its ten-minute limit while it was fetching the repository. Python setup and package replay were skipped. The PR author lacks permission to rerun that upstream job. [Hosted planning job and annotations](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41711798332/job/126182139164)

On a separate Ubuntu 24.04 WSL2 checkout of the exact published commit, CPython 3.12.3 passed the source-history and executable-mode check and all five registered commands. All 28 package files remained byte-identical. The upstream package-selection command selected only this package. The unmodified onboarding command ran 711 tests successfully, including 23 skips.

## Scope and credit

The prices are additive and complete at the stated boundary. The two rank-12 models price top-level dispatch and all positive calls in the fixed trees, respectively. Physical charges and redesigned internal libraries require additional evidence. The proofs and finite checks have one assisted author. Classical knapsack periodicity and residue methods are credited in the proof. The prior compiler and batching work is due to Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv, Mihir Srivastava and Nick Petalas. Prepared for SHIN09-git with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0.

The next source-bound question is whether the actual movement, ownership, precision and internal-call bills for the two rank-eight programs clear the 3,920-to-one threshold.
